name: effectiveness_limited_max_power
title: Effectiveness-limited heat engine at maximum power
summary: Maximum power of an endoreversible heat engine whose heat exchange with the hot and the cold stream is limited by the effectivenesses of its boiler (eff_b) and condenser (eff_cond), from the effectiveness relations of the original; the engine runs at the Curzon-Ahlborn-type efficiency eta_mp = 1 - sqrt(T_C_in/(phi*T_H_in)) with an irreversibility factor phi.

origin.notes: Example 8.6-1 of Klein & Nellis, THERMODYNAMICS, Cambridge University Press, 2011, from the F-Chart Software EES example set. Only the active maximum-power block is imported (hot-fluid inlet through W_dot_max); the toluene Rankine plant of the original sits inside one comment block and PROCEDURE Turbine/Pump are not used by it. Binary source and stored solution from ees-examples-raw/Case_Study/example_8.6-1.eez of the same mirror (commit 5c703d0).

verification.summary: Solved natively in CoolSolve and compared with the EES stored solution of the companion .eez (ees-examples-raw): 25 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); max rel diff 5.7e-08 on m_dot_H (EES stores 7-digit values). The 50 reference-only records (toluene Rankine cycle of the commented block and older runs, e.g. eta_t, eta_p) are out of scope per the card.
verification.reference: Stored solution of ees-examples-raw/Case_Study/example_8.6-1.eez (EES-Community/ees-examples), compared with compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: compare_solution.py output: 25 common variables, 0 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 50; only in CoolSolve: 1 (F$, a string variable with no stored record). Key values, EES vs CoolSolve: W_dot_max 43675.46 vs 43675.46139 W (2.5e-09 rel), eff_b 0.85280146 vs 0.852801480 (1.9e-08), eff_cond 0.95739479 vs 0.957394790 (2.0e-10), eta_mp 0.13036544 vs 0.130365446 (1.0e-09), eta_max 0.24373574 vs 0.243735740 (5.7e-12). Plausibility: eta_mp < eta_max < 1, 0 < eff_b, eff_cond < 1, W_dot_max far below the upper bound eff_cond*C_dot_C*(T_H_in-T_C_in) = 1.64 MW.
